newsitem.title: USA: AMERICAN FOOTBALL-NOTRE DAME NAMES ASSISTANT DAVIES AS COACH.
newsitem.headline: AMERICAN FOOTBALL-NOTRE DAME NAMES ASSISTANT DAVIES AS COACH.

text.p: Notre Dame, American college football's most storied programme, promoted defensive coordinator Bob Davie to head coach to succeed Lou Holtz on Sunday.

The announcement came a day after Holtz coached his final game at South Bend. Holtz, who recommended Davie for the job after resigning last Tuesday, will coach the Fighting Irish for their final regular-season game at Southern California next Saturday and in the post-season bowl game.

"Right now I feel like the luckiest man alive," said Davie. "I'm the head coach at a place I love and a place that represents all that's right in college football. I feel I'm the right guy at this time. I prepared for this for 20 years. It's been well worth the wait."

The announcement capped a flurry of college coaching changes, most notably Gene Stallings' surprise announcement of his retirement as Alabama coach on Saturday and the last game of Carm Cozza's distinguished 32-year caareer at Yale.
Davie was selected unanimously by Notre Dame's three-man selection committee and the recommendation was approved by university president Reverend Edward Molloy.
"This is the greatest university and the best coaching job in America," said Davie. "This place is different and because of that I've come to love Notre Dame."

Davie had been considered the leading candidate to become the new head coach at Purdue, but apparently pulled out when informed he was being offered the Notre Dame job. Purdue hired Wyoming coach Joe Tiller Friday, fuelling speculation that Davie would succeed Holtz at Notre Dame.

Davie has been the defensive coordinator at Notre Dame for the past three seasons. He was the defensive coordinator at Texas A&M for the previous five years (1989-93). Davie has never been a head coach at any level.
"My goals are simple and they coincide with the mission of this university," said Davie.
"Number one is to be the best in everything we do, but to do it with integrity.
"Number two, continue to be the model programme for developing student athletes. Not only graduate them, but develop them as total persons.
"Number three, I want to put a team on the field that represents the very best. We will have a team that plays with great enthusiasm and great desire, but most of all with class."

Notre Dame athletic director Mike Wadsworth confirmed that four candidates were interviewed for the position. Davie, Notre Dame quarterbacks coach Tom Clement and former UCLA coach Terry Donahue were believed to be among those interviewed.

Northwestern coach Gary Barnett was believed to be the leading candidate when Holtz resigned and he has said he was contacted by Notre Dame officials. But Barnett removed his name from consideration Thursday, stressing he never was formally offered the job.
Davie praised Holtz at Sunday's news conference.

"I'd like to thank Lou Holtz," said Davie. "Three years ago when I came here, Lou Holtz told me he he would teach me how to be a head football coach. He did that. No one cared more about Notre Dame and loved this university more than Lou Holtz."

Holtz was a winner in his final game at Notre Dame Stadium Saturday as the 10th-ranked Fighting Irish crushed defenceless Rutgers 62-0. Holtz improved to 100-29-2 as Notre Dame coach, second in wins behind the legendary Knute Rockne.
The 59-year-old Holtz was carried off the field by his players, but stopped to address the sellout crowd at Notre Dame Stadium.
"To be here has been very, very special," Holtz said. "I feel blessed."

"So many great memories, it's been a wonderful experience for me and I'm grateful," Holtz said. "I'll miss the players, the fans, but particularly the students. They've been so good to me, they supported me. I love them."
Notre Dame closes its regular season November 30 at Southern California. The Fighting Irish (8-2) are expected to earn a berth in the bowl alliance if they defeat the Trojans.
